column1: # ---- 04-compliance/T3 ----
Two runs with the same manifest must produce byte-identical outputs, and this is tested rather than asserted.
Reproducibility means the same manifest gives byte-identical artefacts on the same machine, on a different machine, and after an unrelated refactor.
Localisation means that when artefacts differ the Merkle chain names the first upstream artefact that diverged.
Isolation means every recorded seam is a sufficient input for replaying its consumer with no ambient state.
Acyclicity means that within a tick no component reads a value written later in the same tick.
A measured optimality gap between two runs is noise if the runs are not reproducible.
A lookahead audit that asserts the result did not change proves nothing if the result never repeats anyway.
A run is defined by its manifest, nothing outside the manifest may influence output, and anything that does is a defect.
The manifest records the engine's git commit hash plus a dirty-tree flag, and a dirty-tree run's artefacts are marked non-reproducible and cannot be promoted to a golden baseline.
The manifest records the hash of the fully-resolved configuration after all layering and overrides, because layered config is where works-on-my-machine lives.
The manifest records the MarketCalendar hash covering gates, product blocks, holidays, tick and lot sizes and HLZF tables per DSO per year.
The manifest records the pinned IANA tzdata release, because civil time is versioned data.
The manifest records a hash per model artefact: scenario generator, ensemble reduction, value function, fill model, activation model, Tier-3 surface and price-impact curves.
The manifest records the data snapshot as an asOf range and the ingestion watermark, because two runs a day apart see different revisions of the same series unless the watermark is pinned.
The manifest records the solver backend name and version, because the backend is pluggable and the choice is part of the run.
The manifest records solver determinism settings: seed, thread count, deterministic work limit, MIP gap tolerance, presolve and cut settings.
The manifest records the declared lexicographic tie-break rule for degenerate optima, without which degenerate alternates flap.
The manifest records runMode as Reproducibility or Production, which are explicitly different manifests.
manifestId is the hash of every manifest field and is carried in every payload.
An artefact whose manifestId does not match the run that claims to have produced it is a HALT.
Every artefact the run loaded is named in the manifest, and no unlisted environment variable, file or service was read.
The sandbox report is produced by the same instrumentation as the acyclicity audit: the run executes with file, network and clock access mediated and every access recorded.
An undeclared read is a manifest defect.

The per-tick golden record is the tuple of manifestId, tickId and the content hashes of the BeliefSnapshot, ValuationBundle, PlanResult, ExecutionIntent, ExecutionOutcome, SettlementResult and StateUpdate.

The per-run golden record is the hash of the ordered sequence of golden tick rows plus scalar summaries: total objective, total realised P&L, the four error buckets, tier usage counts, mode-transition counts and solve-time percentiles.
The scalar summaries are not the gate; the hashes are, and the scalars exist so a reviewer approving a baseline change can see what moved rather than merely that something did.
The smoke golden scope is one tick on one canonical C1 fixture, run pre-commit within five seconds.

The canonical window golden scope is seven days containing one DST transition, one negative-price episode, one peak-critical day, one high aFRR clearing block and one degraded-feed day, run on every PR within eight minutes.
The full history golden scope is the whole backtest corpus, run nightly and pre-release within three hours.
Because each contract is a serialisable value with no object references, each layer is replayed alone against a recorded seam.
Replaying L2 alone against recorded C1 and StateSnapshot streams and matching the C2 hash proves valuation is a function of belief and state with no Belief store, no network and no clock present.

Replaying L3 alone against recorded C2 and StateSnapshot streams and matching the C3 and PlanResult hashes proves the plan is a function of the primitives and that the Planner never re-derives economics.
Replaying L5 alone against recorded C3 and C4 streams and matching the C5 hash proves Settlement reconstructs truth from outcome alone, uncontaminated by ex-ante belief.
Replaying L1 alone against a cold-tier snapshot and an asOf sequence and matching the C1 hash proves Belief is a pure read and that no-lookahead holds through the whole read path.
Each per-layer replay runs in a stripped host where the Belief store is not constructed, the network stack is unavailable and the clock API throws.
A layer that needs the Belief store, the network or the clock fails immediately and loudly rather than passing by accident because the ambient service happened to be there.
The content hash and input hashes across a tick form a DAG and across a run a chain.
Every artefact's recomputed hash matches its carried contentHash, its inputHashes is non-empty, every input hash resolves to an artefact in the run, and its manifestId matches the run's.
The run's artefact edges are a subset of the declared edges — C1 through C5 plus L0 read and write only — and the edge set is acyclic.
The only backwards edge is from the SettlementResult of one tick to the StateSnapshot of the next.
An artefact whose inputHashes names something the architecture says it cannot depend on is a coupling violation caught by data, before anyone has to read the code.
Divergence localisation walks the ticks in order and the artefacts in topological order, reporting the first artefact whose inputs all agree but whose own hash differs.
Two runs with different manifestIds are not a divergence but a different run.
Everything downstream of the first divergence is a consequence rather than a cause.
The field-level diff is part of the tooling rather than an afterthought, because reporting that a bundle differs is not actionable while reporting the specific term, field and value change is.
The solver is the single largest source of non-determinism and its settings are part of the manifest rather than of the environment.
The reproducibility configuration runs single-threaded while the production configuration runs multi-threaded with the thread count recorded.

The reproducibility configuration expresses its time limit in deterministic work units where the backend supports it, while the production configuration may use wall clock and the manifest records that it does.
Presolve, cuts and heuristics are fixed and explicit in both configurations and never set to auto.
Numerical focus and scaling are fixed in both configurations.
Solving the same model twice under the reproducibility configuration gives byte-identical solutions.
The reproducibility time limit is in deterministic work units unless the backend declares no support and the run mode is Production.
A backend that cannot be deterministic under parallelism runs single-threaded in the reproducibility configuration.
No RNG is constructed in L1 through L5 at runtime, enforced by an analyzer rule, and scenario draws are loaded from an artefact with a recorded seed.
No output-affecting path iterates an unordered collection, enforced by an analyzer over the tick-loop assemblies.
Parallel reductions use a fixed partitioning scheme so summation order is stable regardless of thread scheduling, asserted bit-identical across 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads.
Clock APIs including DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow, Stopwatch used for control flow and Environment.TickCount are banned in the L1 through L5 assemblies.
The clock analyzer has its own test suite with a fixture that must produce the diagnostic and a fixture that must not.
No contract field is populated from a construction-time timestamp, and time enters only as tickId or SlotId and asOf supplied by the driver.
Timing instrumentation is permitted and explicitly carved out: solve-time measurement writes to a side channel excluded from contentHash.
The timing carve-out is narrow and is itself tested, because a timing value that leaks into a hashed field fails the golden comparison immediately, which is the desired outcome.
Production runs with more threads and therefore a different manifest, and this is recorded rather than pretended away.
Production artefacts are compared against production-manifest goldens rather than against reproducibility-manifest goldens.
The reproducibility manifest is the one that gates merges, because it is the only one where a hash difference is unambiguous.
The measured throughput loss of the reproducibility configuration is reported in T5, so the cost of determinism is a number rather than an argument.
The tick's acyclicity is verified mechanically rather than by reading code.
During an instrumented replay every L0 access and every seam access is recorded as tickId, layer, key, direction and sequence.
L0 is accessed through a single instrumented facade in the audit build, so there is no path that escapes recording.

A layer that obtains state by a route other than the instrumented facade produces no record, which is why the audit also asserts that each layer's recorded reads account for the inputs its output depends on.
The acyclicity audit asserts no read of a same-tick write.
The acyclicity audit asserts L0 is read only in the read phase and written only in the write phase, and that the phases do not interleave.
The acyclicity audit asserts only L5 and L3's pending ledger entries write L0 within a tick.
The acyclicity audit asserts seam order is strictly forward from C1 through C5.
The acyclicity audit asserts no layer reads a downstream layer's output within the tick.
The acyclicity audit asserts the state read at the top of the tick is the state written at the end of the previous tick and nothing else.
The previous-tick state assertion catches the subtle version of the bug: not a same-tick read but a stale-by-two-ticks read caused by a caching layer that did not invalidate.
The lag is supposed to be exactly one tick, explicit and priceable, and a lag of two is a different, unpriced system.
Read-set sufficiency perturbs an input a layer did not record reading and asserts the output does not move, then perturbs one it did record and expects the output to move.
A recorded read that never matters is dead weight and is reported as a warning.

A layer whose output changes when an unrecorded input is perturbed is reading something through a path the audit cannot see — a static, a cached singleton, an ambient service — which is precisely the hidden state that destroys the compliance architecture.
The acyclicity audit runs nightly on the canonical window in an instrumented build.
The acyclicity audit is not run in CI because the instrumentation cost is roughly three to five times, and is not run in production at all.
An acyclicity audit failure is a merge blocker for the following day and pages the platform owner, because an acyclicity violation invalidates every per-layer replay taken since the last clean audit.

Hashes-only recording writes golden tick rows and the scalar summaries for every bulk backtest, every CI run and every production tick, retained permanently because a golden tick row is tens of bytes.

Full-seam recording writes every C1 through C5 payload plus PlanResult and StateSnapshot in canonical binary for designated audit days, retained 24 months or until the manifest they belong to is retired.
Full seams plus solver logs and any irreducible infeasible subsystem are recorded on demand for incident investigation, retained 90 days.
The designated-audit-day trigger list is configuration versioned with the calendar.
A day in the canonical CI window is a designated audit day, because it holds the fixtures the whole suite depends on.
A DST transition day is a designated audit day.
An accounting period boundary day is a designated audit day, for the peak reset behaviour.
A peak-critical or qualification-critical day is a designated audit day, because those are the days where the largest downside lives.
A negative-price episode day is a designated audit day, because that is where the simultaneity invariant becomes non-redundant.
A day the engine spent in DEFENSIVE, SAFE or HALT is a designated audit day, because degradation behaviour is only auditable if it was recorded.
A day with a reserve activation above a threshold is a designated audit day, for commitment feasibility under stress.
A day with an unexplained ratio above threshold is a designated audit day, because those are the days that need forensics.
One in N ordinary days is sampled deterministically by hash so the corpus is not composed only of exciting days.
A fixture corpus made entirely of interesting days trains the suite on the tail and lets an ordinary-day regression through.

A recorded seam becomes a permanent test fixture when it is referenced by a test, at which point it is copied into the versioned fixture corpus with its manifest and stops being subject to the retention policy.
Fixtures are content-addressed like any other artefact, so a fixture cannot be edited in place: an updated fixture is a new artefact and the test that references it changes in the same commit.
A golden hash change is either intentional or a regression, and the workflow decides which in a fixed order.
If the manifest differs, the change is not a regression but a different run, and the changed field is identified before classification.
tzdata and calendar changes land as manifest differences regularly and are legitimate, but they still require a reviewed re-baseline.
Step two localises the divergence to the first artefact whose inputs agree and whose own hash differs, with a field-level diff.
If replaying the identified layer alone against the recorded input seam reproduces the divergence, the layer changed.

If the single-layer replay does not reproduce the divergence, it is environmental — threads, iteration order, a floating-point reduction, or an undeclared input — and is re-run under the reproducibility manifest and the sandbox report to find the undeclared read.
The unit of bisection is the single-layer replay rather than the whole backtest, and because it runs in seconds a 200-commit range is about eight replays.

An intentional golden change updates the baseline, and the PR must state which artefact moved, the field-level diff, the scalar summary delta, and why the new value is correct, reviewed by both the layer owner and the platform owner.
A regression is reverted or fixed and the shrunk case becomes a T0 or T2 regression fixture in the same commit.
An environmental divergence is fixed as a determinism defect and never re-baselined around, because a baseline that absorbs non-determinism destroys the ability to detect the next small regression.
A baseline update is a separate commit from the change that caused it, referenced by it, because mixing them makes the history unreadable.
The baseline commit message records the manifest field that changed and the scalar delta, and "updated goldens" is not an acceptable message.
Baselines are never updated on a dirty tree.
More than one baseline update per release is a signal rather than a routine, and the release checklist counts them.
Tolerance-based golden comparison is not allowed, because approximate reproducibility removes the ability to detect small regressions; comparison is on hashes.
Excluding a noisy field from the hash is not allowed, because if a field is non-deterministic the non-determinism is the bug.
The only hash exclusion is the declared timing side-channel, and adding to that list is an ADR-level decision.
Re-baselining to make CI green before a release is not allowed, because the release gate requires the golden state to be explained rather than merely accepted.
